title: EPFO 3.0 Goes Live With UPI Withdrawals and Faster Claim Settlement Under New Rules
excerpt: The overhauled provident fund system allows instant UPI withdrawals up to 75% of balance, auto-settles claims up to Rs 5 lakh, and mandates penalties for delayed processing.
body:
• EPFO 3.0 is now operational with UPI-based PF withdrawals, eliminating the traditional multi-day claim filing process for eligible members.
  • The auto-settlement limit has been raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh, with 71% of advance claims processed within three days in FY26.
  • A mandatory 20-day settlement deadline now applies to all verified claims, with 12% penal interest imposed on officials who cause delays.
  • Members must maintain a minimum 25% balance in their EPF account for retirement security; no employer approval is needed for standard withdrawals.

What's Changed

India's Employees' Provident Fund Organisation has rolled out a sweeping digital overhaul that fundamentally changes how nearly 8 crore subscribers access their retirement savings. Under EPFO 3.0, which became operational with new rules effective June 29, members can withdraw up to 75% of their EPF balance through UPI, bypassing the multi-day paperwork that has frustrated workers for years.

The upgrade introduces auto-claim settlement for amounts up to Rs 5 lakh — a fivefold increase from the previous Rs 1 lakh cap. Claims within this threshold are processed without manual verification, provided the member's Aadhaar, PAN, and bank details are linked and verified with their Universal Account Number.

Speed and Accountability

The numbers show the system is delivering on its promise. In FY26, 71.11% of advance withdrawal claims were settled through auto mode within three days, up from 59.19% the previous year, according to the Labour Ministry.

For claims that require manual review, a strict 20-day settlement deadline now applies. Officials who delay processing face a penal interest charge of 12% per annum on the delayed amount, recoverable from their salary — a provision that adds teeth to what was previously an aspirational timeline.

How It Works

The new system distinguishes between "locked" funds reserved for retirement and "eligible" funds available for withdrawal. Members can access their balance through the UMANG app, generate a QR code, and transfer funds directly to their linked bank account. EPFO is also rolling out EPF-linked ATM cards through tie-ups with 32 public and private sector banks.

Aadhaar-based OTP verification has replaced employer approval for standard withdrawals, cutting out a bottleneck that often added days to the process. The only constraint: a minimum 25% balance must remain in the account at all times to protect long-term retirement security.

Why NRIs Should Pay Attention

The reforms matter for the diaspora because many NRIs still have dormant EPF accounts from previous Indian employment. Under the old system, settling these claims from abroad was notoriously cumbersome. The digital-first approach — with Aadhaar OTP replacing employer sign-off — should simplify the process for overseas claimants, though full UPI access requires an Indian bank account linked to the member's UAN.

What's Next

EPFO manages a corpus of nearly Rs 28 lakh crore. The organisation is gradually expanding UPI withdrawal capabilities and plans to integrate with BHIM and other major UPI platforms. The success of EPFO 3.0 will be measured not just by processing speed but by whether the penal provisions actually reduce the chronic delays that have eroded trust in the system for decades.
nri_angle: NRIs with dormant EPF accounts from prior Indian employment benefit from digital-first claim processing that eliminates employer sign-off.
